items.title: Trial begins for former Central African Republic leader Bozizé over war crimes
items.description: The UN-backed Special Criminal Court in the Central African Republic will on Tuesday, with foreign judges, begin the trial in absentia of former president François Bozizé over crimes against humanity. items.title: Iran's hardliners protest US deal, but the regime closes ranks
items.description: Nicknamed 'the Worried,' the radical wing of the regime denounces the ceasefire protocol with street protests and slogans, calling for revenge against Washington. However, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is backing the agreement, which authorities seek to present as a strategic victory.

items.title: Russia strikes leave historic Kyiv cathedral in flames
items.description: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was set on fire as Russia struck multiple cities in Ukraine overnight. Meanwhile, Moscow reported three deaths from a Ukrainian drone attack.

items.title: Refugee turned peacemaker: The young woman leader transforming communities in the Central African Republic
items.description: In the heart of the Central African Republic (CAR), a nation long marked by conflict, Nina Mireille Yankinon stands as a symbol of resilience, leadership, and hope, dedicating her life to helping communities torn apart by war.
